Fit the latent RSA model family

Source: R/rsa-mplus-family.R
fit_rsa_mplus_family.Rd

Writes, runs, and reads a set of second-order response surface models from one model specification, the latent counterpart of the model family that RSA::RSA() fits. Each model is generated by create_rsa_mplus_model() with its rsa_model; all other arguments are shared. Compare the fitted models with compare_rsa_mplus_models().

Usage

fit_rsa_mplus_family(
  data,
  measurement,
  structural = NULL,
  roles = c(x = "X", y = "Y", outcome = "Z"),
  model_type = c("latent", "si_lms"),
  reliability = NULL,
  constraints = c("surface", "principal"),
  blocks = list(),
  model_extra = NULL,
  constraint_extra = NULL,
  usevariables = NULL,
  identification = c("marker", "effects", "invariance"),
  center = c("none", "pooled"),
  free_intercepts = NULL,
  models = c("full", "SRRR", "SRR", "RR", "SRSQD", "SSQD", "SQD", "IA", "additive",
    "onlyx2", "onlyy2", "onlyx", "onlyy", "null"),
  start = "full",
  modelout,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  Mplus_command = NULL,
  quiet = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing all variables exported to Mplus.

measurement

A named list mapping latent variables to indicators, or a character vector of lavaan/tidySEM measurement statements.

structural

Optional structural model. Supply a named list mapping outcomes to predictors, or a character vector of lavaan/tidySEM paths. The core X and Y paths to the RSA outcome are added when absent.

roles

Named character vector with elements x, y, and outcome identifying the latent variables used in the RSA model.

model_type

Either "latent" for multi-indicator factors or "si_lms" for reliability-corrected single-indicator factors.

reliability

For model_type = "si_lms", a named numeric vector of reliability estimates for the three latent variables in roles.

constraints

Which built-in constraints to include. "surface" produces cs, cc, is, ic, and a5; "principal" additionally produces the stationary point and principal axes for the models that have them (see Details).

blocks

Named list of Mplus input blocks. Values replace defaults for the corresponding block. MODEL and MODELCONSTRAINT are reserved; use model_extra and constraint_extra to extend them. The VARIABLE block may contain additional directives, but USEVARIABLES is generated from usevariables and must not be supplied through blocks.

model_extra

Additional raw statements appended to the Mplus MODEL block.

constraint_extra

Additional raw statements appended to the Mplus MODEL CONSTRAINT block.

usevariables

Character vector of data columns to export and include in the Mplus USEVARIABLES statement. Defaults to all columns in data.

identification

How the X, Y, and outcome factors are scaled, for model_type = "latent". "marker" (default) fixes the first loading of each factor to 1. "effects" uses effects coding (Little, Slegers, & Card, 2006): loadings are constrained to average 1, so each factor is on the metric of its average indicator. This changes the units of b1-b5 slightly but not the fit of the model. "invariance" keeps the marker loadings and puts the X and Y factors on one metric through scalar measurement invariance: the k-th X and Y indicators share their loading and their intercept, the two marker intercepts are fixed at 0, and both factor means are freed. It requires as many X as Y indicators, given in matching order. Unlike "effects", it restricts the model, and it writes no MODEL CONSTRAINT statements for the measurement model, so it also runs under ESTIMATOR = BAYES. See Details.

center

Origin of the X/Y plane. "none" (default) fixes both factor means at 0, so each factor is centred at its own mean and the line X = Y means "both at their average" rather than equality. "pooled", which requires identification = "effects" or "invariance", subtracts one constant (the mean of the X and Y scale means) from every X and Y indicator in a DEFINE statement and frees the two factor means; under effects coding it also constrains the intercepts to sum to zero. X = Y is then equality on the shared response scale, the latent counterpart of RSA::RSA(center = "pooled"). This assumes the X and Y items share a response metric. The move is a translation by the latent mean difference Delta = E(X) - E(Y): b3-b5, a2, a4, and a5 are unchanged, while a3 shifts by -Delta * a4 and a1 by -Delta * a5. User DEFINE statements are placed after the shift.

free_intercepts

For identification = "invariance", names of indicators whose intercept is not shared between X and Y (partial scalar invariance). Naming either member of a matched pair frees the pair. The marker pair cannot be freed.

models

The models to fit, named as rsa_model in create_rsa_mplus_model(). The default is the default set of RSA::RSA(); "mean" and "diff" can be added. The full model is always fitted first.

start

Start values for the polynomial terms. "full" (the default) fits the full model first and uses its estimates for all other models. NULL uses none. Any other value is passed to every model as start in create_rsa_mplus_model().

modelout

Path of an Mplus .inp file that names the family. Each model is written next to it with its name appended in lower case, for example rsa_srrr.inp for modelout = "rsa.inp", and all models read the data file rsa.dat. Mplus lower-cases file names, so on a case-sensitive file system (Linux, WSL) the file name of modelout must be lower case as well.

overwrite

If TRUE, replace existing input and data files. If FALSE (the default), nothing is written when any of them exists.

Mplus_command

Optional path or command used to invoke Mplus.

quiet

If TRUE, suppress status messages from MplusAutomation.

Value

An object of class rsa_mplus_family, a list with

  • models: the named list of workflows (see create_rsa_mplus_model()) in the order fitted. A model that failed in Mplus has status "failed"; one that could not be created is NULL.

  • failures: a data frame with the model, stage, and error message of each failed model.

  • start: the start values passed to the models other than the full model, or NULL.

  • files: the input paths, named by model, and the shared data path.

Details

A model that fails does not stop the others. Each failure is recorded with the stage at which it occurred: "create" (for example, a NEW label that clashes with a label in structural), "write", or "run", where Mplus reported an error. A model whose Mplus output exists keeps its parsed results, so that compare_rsa_mplus_models() can still show what Mplus estimated. A warning lists the failed models. If no model can be generated, the specification itself is invalid and the first error is raised.

The restricted models are nested in the full model and share its measurement model, so start values from the full model mostly save iterations. When the full model fails, the other models are fitted without start values.

See also

compare_rsa_mplus_models()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
family <- fit_rsa_mplus_family(
  data = dat,
  measurement = list(
    X = c("x1", "x2", "x3"),
    Y = c("y1", "y2", "y3"),
    Z = c("z1", "z2", "z3")
  ),
  modelout = "family/rsa.inp"
)
compare_rsa_mplus_models(family)
RSA_mplus(family$models$SRRR)
} # }
